phrase:
I’m digging through the trash
For a hard drive
note: Welsh IT worker James Howells threw away a hard drive holding about 8,000 bitcoin in 2013. He spent years trying to dig it out of a Newport landfill before UK courts ruled against him in 2025.
In 2021 El Salvador became the first country to make bitcoin legal tender. A 2025 change tied to an IMF loan made accepting it voluntary for businesses.

phrase:
I’ll remember 12 words
From my past life
note: A seed phrase is a list of 12 or 24 words that can restore a bitcoin wallet anywhere. Remember them and the coins survive even if every device is lost.
Hopium, hope plus opium, is crypto slang for comforting optimism that prices will bounce back, whether or not the evidence agrees.
FUD stands for fear, uncertainty and doubt. FUDsters spread scary claims about Bitcoin, sometimes sincerely, sometimes to shake people into selling.

phrase:
I’ll sell my diamond hands
To buy more sats
note: Diamond hands means holding through any crash without selling. Sats are satoshis, bitcoin's smallest unit: one hundred-millionth of a coin.

phrase: Stack ASICs on some tall racks
note: ASICs are computers built for one job: Bitcoin mining. Miners rack thousands of them, competing to add the next block of transactions and earn new bitcoin.

phrase:
If bears hibernate
I’m calling that a long nap
note: A bear market is a long stretch of falling prices. When the bears 'hibernate', the market goes quiet and sideways, sometimes for months.

phrase:
Half a milly
What hashrate foretells
note: 'Half a milly' is a US$500,000 bitcoin. Hashrate is the total computing power securing the network; bulls read rising hashrate as miners investing heavily because they expect higher prices.
A doof is Australian slang for a dance party with thumping electronic music, named after the 'doof doof' of the bass.
Being orange-pilled means becoming convinced about Bitcoin, a play on the red pill in The Matrix, with orange for Bitcoin's logo.

phrase:
Cause we just made toxic maxis
Radioactive
note: 'Toxic maxis' are Bitcoin maximalists known for blunt, uncompromising defence of Bitcoin and rejection of other cryptocurrencies. Radioactive is the next level of toxic.
A fiat maxi trusts only government-issued money, the mirror image of a Bitcoin maximalist.

The Sovereign Individual (1997), by James Dale Davidson and William Rees-Mogg, predicted that digital money would weaken governments' grip and shift power to individuals. Many Bitcoiners treat it as a prophecy.
Money stores the hours you worked. When inflation shrinks its buying power, those hours are quietly taken, so Bitcoiners call money printers time thieves.

phrase:
Operate on block time
With ten minute intervals
note: Bitcoin adds a new block of transactions roughly every ten minutes. 'Block time' is the network's own clock, counted in blocks rather than calendar dates.

phrase: Hashrate at an all time high
note: A record hashrate means more computing power than ever is protecting Bitcoin, making any attack on the network more expensive.

phrase: As we opt out and we exit
note: Opting out, or 'exit', means leaving a system instead of fighting it: moving savings from fiat into money no central authority controls.
The genesis block is Bitcoin's first block, mined in January 2009. It contains a newspaper headline: 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks'.

phrase:
Of a paper Nakamoto wrote
Just 9 pages to inspire
note: The Bitcoin white paper, published by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto on 31 October 2008, is just nine pages long, and it describes the entire system.
Pupusas are El Salvador's national dish: thick corn tortillas stuffed with cheese, beans or pork.
Martin Luther King Jr's 1963 'I Have a Dream' speech called for equality for all. Bitcoin's version is money with the same rules for every user.
Cold storage means keeping bitcoin keys completely offline, on a hardware wallet or written down, out of reach of online hackers.
Consensus is how thousands of independent computers agree on one shared record of who owns what: everyone runs the same rules, and no one is in charge.

phrase:
Because they tried
To tweak the model
note: Changing Bitcoin's rules needs broad agreement. In the 'block size wars', a push for bigger blocks failed to win users over, and its backers split off in 2017 to create Bitcoin Cash.
